page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-1GB is an entry-level virtual server powered by KVM virtualization. The instance is provisioned with a single shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, SHA-NI, and VAES. System memory is sized at 1.0 GB, yielding a 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Hardware bundling includes 25 GB of local SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The server operates without discrete GPU acceleration. Because CPU resources are allocated on a shared basis, performance is constrained by total thread capacity. Synthetic evaluation reflects this profile: stress-ng single-core execution delivers a top-tier score of 3,776.07, demonstrating modern Zen architecture efficiency, yet aggregate multi-core throughput and PassMark scores remain in lower quartiles due to the solitary virtual core.

Data throughput metrics illustrate an entry-tier envelope. Single-threaded gzip compression achieves 28.17 GB/s and large-block memory writes reach 31.65 GB/s, both representing mid-tier performance. In contrast, uncached read bandwidth drops to 36.28 GB/s and static web serving throughput measures 5.58 GB/s. Redis SET operations reach 2.87 million operations per second, while LLM text generation on a lightweight 135M model sustains 88.97 tokens per second.

The constrained memory footprint of 1.0 GB limits the instance to lightweight workloads. UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-1GB is suited for low-traffic web proxies, basic background monitoring, utility scripts, configuration management nodes, and development sandboxes where cost-conscious resource allocation takes precedence over sustained multi-threaded performance.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-1GB is a compact virtual machine instance configured with 1 shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 1.0 GB of RAM, a bundled 25 GB local SSD, and one public IPv4 address, operating without dedicated GPU acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile single-core performance in stress-ng at 3,776.07 points, while multi-core metrics and overall system throughput remain constrained by the single-thread, shared-CPU topology. Memory bandwidth yields 31.65 GB/s on large-block writes and gzip compression sustains 28.17 GB/s. Due to its limited 1.0 GB memory capacity and modest aggregate throughput, this instance is suited for lightweight background services, microservices, minimal web proxies, and developer test environments.
